html:
SMTO-EML-0007 — Your email's recipients or sender address weren't accepted

GUID: 96a8dfd2-a89b-5c2d-ab9e-43175b2f0389
Slug: email-recipient-count-invalid
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • Either the email had no recipients or too many, or the mail server refused the sender address or every recipient. The message was not sent to anyone.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the email has at least one recipient and no more than 100 addresses in total across To, Cc and Bcc. SMTO sends each email to between 1 and 100 recipients.
  2. Check each recipient address for typos, and that those mailboxes exist and can receive email from your organization. The mail server refuses addresses it can't deliver to, and when it refuses all of them nothing is sent.
  3. If the sender address was refused, open Parameter Store, select your email sender profile, and make sure its sender address is one this mailbox is allowed to send as. Mail servers refuse to send from an address the signed-in account doesn't own or have permission to use.
  4. Ask SMTO to send the email again with the corrected addresses. The server refused the email before receiving its content, so sending again after the fix won't create a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message for your recipients.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your email administrator; they include the mail server's response code for each refused address. Don't switch the sender to someone else's mailbox to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Recipient validation rejected an empty, over-100-entry or duplicate recipient list, or the SMTP server rejected MAIL FROM or every RCPT TO, before any message data was sent.

What this means

  • Local recipient validation rejects an empty, excessive or duplicate envelope, SMTP rejects MAIL FROM, or every RCPT TO is rejected. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • Local recipient validation rejects an empty, excessive or duplicate envelope, SMTP rejects MAIL FROM, or every RCPT TO is rejected.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish local list validation from server sender rejection and all-recipient rejection; partial acceptance has separate receipt evidence.

How to fix it

  • Read error_kind: email_recipient_count_invalid (no recipients, more than 100 to/cc/bcc entries, or duplicates in the envelope), email_sender_rejected (MAIL FROM non-250; check send-as rights for the profile's from_email or envelope_from), or email_all_recipients_rejected (inspect rejected_recipients[].smtp_response_code). Correct the to/cc/bcc arguments or the profile's from_email/envelope_from.
  • Review fixed sender permission and recipient addresses. A send supports at most 100 recipient entries.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended envelope validates and the server's accepted/rejected recipient facts are retained.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
